channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Eyes further losses near $88.50, two-week low amid easing supply risk
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – retains a negative bias for the fifth straight day on Wednesday, flirting with an over two-week low touched on Tuesday.

item.title: USD/IDR Price Forecast: Falls toward moving averages near 17,800 ahead of BI decision
item.description: USD/IDR extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 17,820 during Asian hours on Wednesday. Technical analysis of the daily chart suggests the pair remains within the ascending channel, indicating an ongoing bullish bias.

item.title: Gold edges lower on Fed-driven USD strength as markets await Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to capitalize on the previous day's goodish rebound from sub-$4,300 levels and meets with a fresh supply during the Asian session on Wednesday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index jumps to near 100.70 as Fed maintains hawkish rhetoric
item.description: The US Dollar reflects strength on Wednesday amid firm expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will deliver more interest rate hikes this year.

item.title: Asian stocks trade mixed, Taiwan’s Taiex leads on tech boost
item.description: Asian equities trade mixed on Wednesday. Oil prices and Treasury yields dropped as crude flows through the Middle East improved, adding to risk appetite.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $66.50 as Fed signals further rate hikes
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) depreciates after registering gains the previous day, trading around $66.50 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Wednesday. Non-yielding Silver faces challenges due to the Federal Reserve's hawkish monetary policy outlook.

item.title: Japanese Yen softens on BoJ's lack of hawkish guidance, potential intervention eyed
item.description: The USD/JPY pair gathers strength to around 157.60 during the early Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) extends the decline due to a lack of explicitly hawkish guidance from the Bank of Japan (BoJ) after the rate hike last week.

item.title: Canadian Dollar seems vulnerable as Iran diplomacy hopes weigh on oil prices
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts buyers for the third straight day and trades around the 1.4070-1.4075 area during the Asian session on Wednesday, near its highest level since July 29, touched the previous day.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains under pressure as PMI slows
item.description: AUD/USD loses ground for the third consecutive day, trading around 0.7110 during Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro weakens below 1.1450 on hawkish Fed signals, German political risks
item.description: The EUR/USD pair loses ground to near 1.1445 during the early Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the Euro (EUR) on the hawkish stance of the US Federal Reserve (Fed) and the prospect of further interest rate hikes.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7468 vs. 6.7459 previous
item.description: On Wednesday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7468 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7459 and 6.6971 Reuters estimate.

item.title: British Pound hangs near late July lows vs USD; looks to UK/US PMIs for fresh impetus
item.description: The GBP/USD pair struggles to build on the previous day's modest bounce from the 1.3320 area, or its lowest since July 29, and sticks to a negative bias for the third straight day on Wednesday.

item.title: US Special Envoy Witkoff says mediators completed round of US-Iran talks
item.description: United States (US) Special Envoy to the Middle East, Steve Witkoff, said the US held "lengthy" indirect talks with the Iranian delegation via mediators on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), Reuters reported on Tuesday.

item.title: WTI slumps to near $89.00 as markets weigh Trump’s UN speech
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $89.00 during the early Asian trading hours on Wednesday. WTI falls after US President Donald Trump said the United States (US) held hours-long talks with Iran.

item.title: Explosion heard near Iran’s Qeshm Island
item.description: An explosion was heard near Qeshm Island in southern Iran's Hormozgan province, the official news agency IRNA reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold recovers above $4,350 on US–Iran diplomacy hopes
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rebounds to near $4,360 during the early Asian session on Wednesday. The precious metal edges higher amid hopes for diplomatic progress between the US and Iran.

item.title: 49.3: Australia’s S&P Global Manufacturing PMI declines in September
item.description: The preliminary reading of Australia's S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) eased to 49.3 in September versus 52.0 prior, the latest data published by S&P Global showed on Wednesday.

item.title: The New Zealand Dollar dips to a new low and bounces as Crude Oil gets cheaper
item.description: Four weeks of selling have taken NZD/USD from just under 0.6000 to its lowest since early July. On Tuesday the pair dipped under 0.5700, then climbed back into the 0.5700 to 0.5800 range it has traded in since September 16, and it's trading in the lower half of that range.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains subdued as Fed and RBA hawks collide
item.description: The Aussie Dollar is poised to end Tuesday’s session unchanged versus the Greenback amid renewed hopes for an end of the Middle East conflict, while Federal Reserve officials struck a hawkish tone in their speeches. The AUD/USD trades at 0.7114, near Tuesday’s opening price.

item.title: The Japanese Yen spikes and unwinds as Iran offers to reopen Hormuz
item.description: Cheaper Crude Oil should help the Yen, since Japan buys almost all of its Crude Oil abroad, and on Tuesday it helped only briefly. USD/JPY dropped close to 157.00 after reports that Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, then climbed back to trade near 157.50.

item.title: The Euro drops to its lowest since July as the Dollar keeps climbing
item.description: About 80% of the Euro's August rally is gone. EUR/USD climbed from near 1.1350 at the end of July to just above 1.1700 in the second half of August, and on Tuesday it dipped under 1.1450 to its lowest since late July before recovering to trade near that level.

item.title: The British Pound sets a new September low as Fed officials argue for more
item.description: 1.3400 has capped GBP/USD in every session since the Fed raised rates on September 16. The pair went through that level on the day of the decision and has failed to get back above it four times since.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: RMB gains hinge on PBoC fix – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that the Renminbi (RMB) has extended gains, with USD/CNY breaking below 6.70 as the People's Bank of China (PBoC) strengthened the fix for nine straight sessions ahead of the Trump–Xi meeting.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Sideways bias holds above support against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann maintain a constructive short-term view on USD/SGD, noting recent sideways trade around 1.2760.

item.title: Banxico expected to stay put as inflation risks block easing – Reuters
item.description: A Reuters poll shows that all economists expect that the Mexican Central Bank (Banxico) will hold rates unchanged at 6.50% for the third straight meeting on Thursday.

item.title: ECB’s Nagel says restrictive policy cannot be ruled out
item.description: The Bundesbank President and European Central Bank (ECB) member Joachim Nagel crossed the wires at a financial event in London on Tuesday, acknowledging that high energy prices had driven inflation off its 2026 target.

item.title: Mexican Peso carry cushion thins as USD/MXN breaks 100-day SMA
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) extended its losses for the third straight trading session on Tuesday, down over 0.4% as investors reduce their exposure to the Mexican currency following last week’s Federal Reserve (Fed) decision to raise interest rates.

item.title: South Korean Won: Export surge supports BoK stance – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank reports South Korea’s exports for the first 20 days of September jumped 78.3% year-on-year, extending nine months of double-digit growth and led by a 259% surge in semiconductor exports.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar: Equity inflows support TWD againt US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the Taiwan Dollar (TWD) has extended gains, briefly strengthening near 31.71 versus the US Dollar (USD), supported by strong foreign portfolio inflows and domestic equity outperformance tied to tech and AI themes.

item.title: Gold losses altitude as peace hopes meet hawkish Fed bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price retreats from daily highs of $4,376 on Tuesday as US Treasury yields rise and the US Dollar continues to strengthen, with investors pricing in further Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening towards year-end. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades at $4,337, down 0.14%.
